newsitem.title: USA: IBM to enhance top of the line mainframes.
newsitem.headline: IBM to enhance top of the line mainframes.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp said that it is enhancing the top of the line of its mainframe computers with speedier processors that are almost 10 percent faster than the current processors.

IBM said that because of improvements in its chip manufacturing process and yields, it is able get faster performance from the processors that are the core chips of its mainframes. These processors will be more expensive than previous models but IBM did not give any details on pricing.
IBM emphasized that the faster mainframes, which are the 10-way processor models of its newest System 390 mainframes, are available only in limited quantities.
Analysts estimate that its fastest mainframe processors will now run at speeds of 55 million instructions per second, up from 45 million instructions per second.

Mainframes are still a very important hardware product for IBM, even though their revenues are in decline, because of heavy pricing pressures. But mainframes are still one of the most profitable hardware products for IBM and they also fuel sales of mainframe software, services and maintenance.
Jay Stevens, a Dean Witter analyst, said that because IBM is accelerating its product development cycle in mainframes, it makes it easier to forecast mainframe revenues.
"There are no peaks and valleys...it makes our forecast more reliable," Stevens said.

As a result, last Friday, Stevens raised his price target on the computer giant's stock to $172 from $160, joining two other analysts who recently raised their price targets on IBM, fueling a frenzy on Wall Street for IBM shares.
